analysis: The only changed lines are in the test file PlacementSetupCheck.swift (head lines 1260-1264). The test call to ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine now passes a new argument, publicModels: [], and the assertion message says records only, no public declaration. This is a test-only adaptation to a changed publicTrafficLine signature, which implies a new public-declaration input in production code that is not in the supplied batch. The new publicModels parameter and its semantics are in unseen source. I could not verify that a model with passing records but no public declaration is never treated as publicly qualified. The test expects `.pipeline` to return notYetQualified and `.phaseSplit` to return a line starting with "qualified for public traffic" even with empty publicModels. That means record-derived qualification still yields the qualified line without a public declaration. That may be intended wording for a records-only status line, or it may be a gap if the line drives routing. The production definition and callers should be checked to confirm the line is informational only and does not gate public serving. Related threats are T-052, T-054 and TB-011, which cover a diagnostic or label being mistaken for serving authorization. The rest of the supplied test code (placement, grants, chunk selection, speculative credit, owner pilot) is synthetic fixtures with no secrets, no network or file-system effects, and no new attack surface. Owner-pilot expectations confirm that unqualified models state "Not yet qualified for public traffic" and that there is no public grant for registered_gemma4_26b. No finding is raised on this test-only evidence. The production side of the publicModels change is not visible here.
